statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is low at 4 because CME equity index futures remain halted for the weekend and no tradable Nasdaq-100 price path exists inside any hour of this 24-hour horizon; Stress edges to 39, moderate, as an overnight Ukrainian strike on a Russian refinery adds unpriced energy-supply risk to the newly effective US tariffs on Canadian goods.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion: cash NDX retraced both of its extremes, closed below its own open, and left VIX near session lows at 14.89, while the August expiry cleared without one-way extension. The venue has been shut since 21:00Z Friday and reopens Sunday at 22:00Z, roughly fourteen hours beyond the end of this horizon, so the published Tail describes the absence of a price path rather than an improvement in the backdrop. Two weekend developments are carried as Stress rather than Tail because no market could price them. The US-Canada tariff order took effect at 12:01am ET, covering roughly $20bn of Canadian goods including electronics, industrial machinery and dairy on top of existing steel, lumber and auto tariffs, with Prime Minister Carney suspending negotiations, stating Canada will match dollar for dollar and describing further measures in the coming days. Separately, an overnight drone attack set fire to the Novokuibyshevsk refinery in Samara Oblast, one of Russia's ten largest at about 8.8m tonnes a year, alongside a logistics centre. The rest of the backdrop is re-verified and unchanged: the 2Y/10Y/30Y curve at 4.24%/4.74%/5.28% at Friday's close, WTI at 87.06 and Brent at 94.39 after a second consecutive weekly gain above 5%, and a week-ahead stack of Core PCE and the second Q2 GDP estimate on Wednesday, Nvidia after the Wednesday close and Chair Warsh at Jackson Hole on Friday. One Monday checkpoint firmed this hour: the Treasury press conference detailing measures against Iran now has a published time of 2pm ET, 18:00Z. None of it falls inside the hours published here.
headline: Eighth consecutive closed-venue assessment: CME equity index futures stay halted across every published hour, while an overnight Ukrainian refinery strike joins the newly effective 50% US tariffs on Canadian goods to lift Stress to 39 with Tail unchanged at the closed-venue floor.
body:
CME equity index futures stopped trading for the week at 21:00Z on Friday and reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z, so the venue is confirmed shut across all twenty-four slots published here, which run to 2026-08-23T07:00:00Z. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86, up 95.69 points or 0.33% from a 29,213.17 previous close, after opening at 29,359.60, trading down to 29,142.44, reclaiming the entire decline to 29,405.12 and then handing back roughly ninety-six points to finish below its own open. Both extremes were retraced, neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, and the August expiry cleared without one-way structure. That settlement is corroborated by separately reported Friday index moves: the S&P 500 at 7,674.37, +0.4%, the Nasdaq Composite at 26,180.45, +0.4%, and the Dow at 53,277.01, +1%, with all three indexes still posting weekly losses after the bond selloff earlier in the week. VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.00% from 15.84 and near the low end of a 14.77-15.95 range.

Two verified weekend developments sit outside any tradable session. First, the US-Canada trade escalation completed: negotiations were suspended late Friday and 50% US tariffs on roughly $20bn of Canadian goods took effect at 12:01am ET on Saturday, covering electronics, industrial machinery and dairy products on top of existing steel, lumber and auto measures, with the Prime Minister's office stating that Canada will match those tariffs dollar for dollar and that supporting measures for workers and businesses will follow in the coming days. The Canadian countermeasures are therefore announced but not yet implemented. Second, an overnight drone attack on the night of 21-22 August set fire to the Novokuibyshevsk oil refinery in Samara Oblast, a Rosneft facility processing about 8.8 million tonnes a year and among Russia's ten largest, together with an Ozon logistics centre from which more than 500 employees were evacuated. Both items raise the weight of the eventual Sunday repricing and neither can create an observable Nasdaq-100 price path inside this horizon.

The carried backdrop is rates-led rather than equity-led. Friday closes put the 30-year at 5.28%, near its highest since 2007, the 10-year at 4.74% after testing 20-month highs, and the 2-year at 4.24%; the Federal Reserve H.15 release for 20 August lists 4.19%, 4.69% and 5.23% for the same tenors, the most recent official daily observation. Last week's defining feature was bond volatility, with a Treasury support measure for long-duration debt fully erased within a day. Crude held its war-premium levels, with WTI at 87.06 and Brent at 94.39 after both benchmarks gained more than 5% for a second consecutive week, while Strait of Hormuz transit volumes remain far below pre-conflict levels. The US-Iran impasse is unresolved and the Treasury press conference detailing coordinated economic-isolation measures is now confirmed for Monday at 2pm ET, 18:00Z, with reporting also placing a 60-day ceasefire expiry on the same day.

Cross-asset context collected at 08:12Z is complete and internally consistent but explicitly latest-session and delayed, so it is used only as confirmation: index futures marks of NQ +0.30%, ES +0.38% and YM +0.95% with VIX futures -1.68% reproduce Friday's close rather than any live path. Breadth was mixed rather than aligned, with application and infrastructure software both above 1% while the semiconductor group averaged negative and Nvidia fell 0.98%, which reduces directional conviction rather than amplifying Tail. No amplifier of the kind that would justify a higher Tail is present, because none can be observed while no venue prints a price.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is close to complete: 20 hourly assessments are available and 4 clock-hours have no published assessment and are marked unavailable, two in the 21 August late-morning window and two in the 22 August pre-dawn window. Across the available hours Tail held a narrow 4-16 band and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON throughout. The path is coherent: 12 through the European morning, a drift to 16 into the 14:00Z US cash-open window with a brief event/whipsaw mode around the August expiry, a return to the low teens through the afternoon, then a step down to 10, 5 and finally 4 as the venue moved into its 21:00Z Friday halt and stayed there. Stress traced the same arc in reverse scale, easing from the high fifties to the mid thirties as equity-structure risk was replaced by carried rates, energy and weekend headline risk, with the final available hour at 38 after the tariff order. No danger window was published in any of those hours.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. All twenty-three remaining slots describe the same closed market: the final slot begins at 2026-08-23T07:00:00Z and ends fourteen hours before the Sunday 22:00Z futures reopen, so no live evidence can arrive before this forecast expires. Tail therefore holds a flat closed-venue floor of 4 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON in every slot. Stress opens at 39, one step above the previous hour because the overnight Ukrainian strike on the Novokuibyshevsk refinery adds unpriced energy-supply risk to the already effective US tariffs on Canadian goods, eases to a 37 trough through the quietest Saturday hours, and then climbs to 45 by the final slots as the stock of unpriced weekend information grows and the distance to the reopen shortens. Its composition is the tariff exchange with Canadian countermeasures still pending, the 30-year at 5.28% near a 2007 high, the 10-year at 4.74% after testing 20-month highs, crude near 87.06 WTI and 94.39 Brent, and an unresolved US-Iran impasse with a Monday 18:00Z Treasury announcement outstanding. Confidence starts at 87 and decays to 79 by the final slot as the verified Friday dataset ages; the closed-venue conclusion itself stays effectively certain throughout. Dominant mode is normal in every slot. The first genuine test arrives beyond this horizon, at the Sunday reopen and then Monday's scheduled items, and will be scored on observed structure rather than assumed in advance.
